facts.text: Ann Rinaldi’s 2002 novel "The Coffin Quilt" dramatizes the Hatfield–McCoy feud, bringing the historic conflict to a new generation of readers.
Kevin Costner stars as Devil Anse Hatfield in the History Channel’s three‑part miniseries "Hatfields & McCoys," a dramatization that captured millions of viewers.
The History Channel premiered the reality series "Hatfields & McCoys: White Lightning" on August 1, 2013, revisiting the feud with a modern lens.
Larkin "Lark" McCoy, Asa McCoy’s second son, was ambushed by a West Virginia posse led by the Hatfields, a pivotal moment in the feud’s escalation.
In the 2011 game "Cactus McCoy and the Curse of Thorns," characters Cactus McCoy and Hex Hatfield nod to the historic feud in a playful way.
A 1999 federal grant funded the Hatfield–McCoy Historic Site Restoration, preserving key locations tied to the legendary Appalachian conflict.
